personas.name: high-grade-malignancy-linked-request-major-not-critical
personas.description: A poorly-differentiated malignancy with clear resection margins and a properly linked originating request — a real, verified gotcha in hasCriticalFinding(): a critical finding requires EITHER an involved margin OR an 'unexpected' malignancy specifically defined as malignancyPresent with no originating request reference. Because the request reference IS linked here, this high-grade cancer is graded severity 'major' (R-SEV-MAJOR-02, the high-grade-malignancy path, not the critical-finding path) but classification stays 'abnormal' and follow-up is 'urgent' (within 1 week) rather than 'critical-alert' (immediate) — the exact same tumour grade produces a different classification and urgency purely based on whether the referral was linked, confirmed by direct contrast with the next persona.

state.microscopicDescription: Infiltrating ductal carcinoma with poor glandular differentiation, high nuclear pleomorphism, and a high mitotic count.
state.diagnosis: Invasive ductal carcinoma of the breast, poorly-differentiated (Grade 3).
state.immunohistochemistry: ER positive, PR positive, HER2 negative
state.impression: Poorly-differentiated invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR positive, HER2 negative.

personas.name: high-grade-malignancy-unlinked-request-critical
personas.description: The identical poorly-differentiated malignancy and clear margins as the previous persona, but with no originating request reference recorded — this alone flips hasCriticalFinding() to true (an 'unexpected malignancy'), so classification becomes 'critical' via R-SEV-MAJOR-01 (the critical-finding severity path, not R-SEV-MAJOR-02), and follow-up escalates to 'critical-alert' / immediate. Also raises F-DISCREPANCY-001 (malignancy with no linked request) alongside the two universal critical-result flags — the direct, verified contrast with the persona above.

personas.name: involved-margin-low-grade-tumour-critical
personas.description: A well-differentiated (low-grade) malignancy with an INVOLVED resection margin and a properly linked request — demonstrates that an involved margin overrides even the lowest tumour grade: hasInvolvedMargin() alone makes hasCriticalFinding() true regardless of malignancyPresent's grade weight, so severity resolves to major via R-SEV-MAJOR-01 (critical-finding) rather than R-SEV-MINOR-01 (which a well-differentiated tumour would otherwise reach). Raises F-ABNORMAL-ACTION-001, the margin-specific flag, alongside the two universal critical-result flags.

personas.name: close-margin-lymphovascular-invasion-overrides-low-grade
personas.description: A well-differentiated (low-grade) malignancy that would normally grade minor, but with BOTH a close resection margin and lymphovascular invasion present — the actionable-finding rule (R-SEV-MODERATE-02) takes precedence over the low-grade weight in the severity ladder's evaluation order, so severity resolves to moderate rather than minor. Raises F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001 (malignancy with lymphovascular invasion).
